chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Umm Saʿīd al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said:

I went to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) and entered upon him. The bondmaid came and said, 'I have brought the beast of burden.' He said to me, 'O Umm Saʿīd! What is this beast for? Where do you intend to go?' I said, 'I am going to visit the graves of the martyrs.' He said, 'Postpone it for today. How strange are you, O people of Iraq! You come to the martyrs from a distant journey, but you leave the Master of the Martyrs and do not go to him.' I said to him, 'Who is the Master of the Martyrs?' He said, 'Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī (peace be upon him).' I said, 'I am a woman.' He said, 'There is no harm for one like you to go to him and visit him.' I said, 'What is for us in visiting him?' He said, 'It equals one Ḥajj and one ʿUmrah, and ʿItikāf (seclusion) for two months in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and fasting them, and its goodness is so and so.' She said, 'And he extended his hand and closed it three times.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) according to Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (a.s.) highlights the preeminence of Ḥusayn (a.s.) as the 'Master of the Martyrs' (Sayyid al-Shuhadā'), urging the people of Iraq not to neglect his grave while visiting others. The Imam quantifies the spiritual merit of this visitation as equivalent to a complete Hajj, an Umrah, and two months of I'tikaf with fasting in the Sacred Mosque, emphasizing its sufficiency for a woman’s pilgrimage. This narration underscores the Shia theological view of the Ahl al-Bayt’s graves as focal points of divine grace and intercession.
